Q: . Could you state your full name for us, please, Ms. Flowers?
A: . Sarah Owen Flowers.

Q: . Ms. Flowers, my name is Tommy Roebig. I'm a lawyer. I'm present today with my partner Sarah Bartlett. We represent Carol Taylor and Sheldon Faulk in a case against the Defendant named Socorro and Global Pioneer. Have you ever had your deposition taken before?
A: . Not before today.

Q: . Okay. So I'm going to ask you a series of questions. If you don't understand one of my questions, will you tell me that and I'll try to do better to ask you a question that you do understand?
A: . Sure.

Q: . Okay. And if you don't hear me fully, don't answer the question. Just tell me you didn't hear me. Okay?
A: . Sure.

Q: . If at any time if you want to take a break for any reason, just let us know that and we'll try to accommodate you. Alright?
A: . Alright.

Q: . Last thought, if you in response to one of my questions today want to say yes or no but instead say uh-huh or unh-unh, I'm going to know exactly what you mean. But the transcript won't read correctly. So I may prompt you to say yes or no. I don't mean to be rude or disrespectful if I do that. Okay?
A: . Understood.

Q: . Let's start off with where you work.
A: . I work at Bill Costello's State Farm, Costello Insurance and Financial Services, Incorporated.

Q: . Okay. And you said you work for Bill Costello's State Farm. What is that actually? MR. SHAW: Object to form. Go ahead. BY THE DEPONENT:
A: . I don't know. THE DEPONENT: What was that? Sorry. MR. SHAW: Ignore me. MR. ROEBIG: Some times throughout the afternoon the lawyers are going to make objections to protect their record. And we don't mean to disturb your thought process or get in your way. But you can go ahead and answer if you remember the question. THE DEPONENT: Would you repeat it, please? MR. ROEBIG: Sure. I asked you where you work. You said Bill Costello State Farm, Bill Costello Financial Services. BY MR. ROEBIG:

Q: . My question to you is what is that business? What do they do? MR. SHAW: Object to form. Go ahead. THE DEPONENT: I can answer? MR. ROEBIG: Yes. THE DEPONENT: Okay. What do we do here at this office? Is that what you're asking? MR. ROEBIG: Yeah. BY THE DEPONENT:
A: . We help customers with various insurance products as well as potentially some mutual funds and some other products. BY MR. ROEBIG:

Q: . One of things that you do is sell insurance. Is that right? THE DEPONENT: I'm sorry? BY MR. ROEBIG: . One of the things you do is sell insurance. Is that correct?
A: . That's correct.

Q: . Are you licensed yourself to do that --
A: . Yes.

Q: . -- through the State of Florida?
A: . Yes.

Q: . What does that licensure allow you to do?
A: . It allows me to talk with people about various insurance products and help them start an auto policy for example or a homeowners insurance policy, life insurance policy to name a few.

Q: . Alright. When did you become licensed?
A: . I became licensed originally in 2010.

Q: . 2005?
A: . 2010.

Q: . 2010. You said originally. Does that mean there's been some change in your licensure?
A: . I had to get licenses in Florida when I moved to Florida.

Q: . Okay. So when you were originally licensed in 2010 it was not in Florida?
A: . Correct.

Q: . Where was it?
A: . Kentucky.

Q: . Okay. Did you relinquish those licenses when you left Kentucky?
A: . Yes.

Q: . And when did you become licensed in Florida?
A: . In 2011.

Q: . Alright. Has that license been in full force and effect since --
A: . Yes.

Q: . -- 2011?
A: . Yes.

Q: . And which licensure do you have?
A: . I have -- technically in Florida they refer to it as a 220 and a 215 for life and health.

Q: . And you hold a 220 license?
A: . Yes.

Q: . Okay. Now, with regard to the agency that you work at -- is it an agency? Is that how it's referred to?
A: . That's how it's referred to. Yes.

Q: . Okay. Do you as an employee of the Costello firm sell any insurance in the automobile field but for State Farm Insurance?
A: . It is only State Farm.

Q: . Okay. Is it only State Farm across the whole line of products of insurance that you sell?
A: . The only other company that I can do insurance through would be a flood policy through the National Flood Insurance Program.

Q: . And excepting the national flood coverage all of the other products of an insuring nature are via State Farm?
A: . Yes.

Q: . Okay. Is that what's referred to in your business as being a captive agent?
A: . I'm not familiar with the captive agent term.

Q: . Okay. You have an exclusive relationship with State Farm and you don't sell any products but State Farm products? MR. SHAW: Object to form. Go ahead. BY MR. ROEBIG: . Is that right? THE DEPONENT: I don't understand what you mean by that question. BY MR. ROEBIG: . Can you sell products from Aetna, Progressive or Allstate?
A: . No.

Q: . Because you have an agreement with State Farm that you will not do that. Is that right?
A: . I don't know what the agreement is. I just know that I cannot sell those other policies that you had mentioned.

Q: . Okay. How is it that you know that?
A: . It's been told to me.

Q: . By your employer?
A: . Yes.

Q: . Okay. Did you have to go through some training at State Farm to be an exclusive salesperson for their insuring products? MR. SHAW: Object to form. BY THE DEPONENT:
A: . There is some training when you start with a State Farm agent. BY MR. ROEBIG:

Q: . There's some training when you start with a State Farm agent? Is that what you said?
A: . There is -- yes. There's some training when I started in this office working for Costello Insurance and Financial Services.

Q: . The question actually is did you have any training from State Farm?
A: . I have access to information on our computer system for some training.

Q: . From State Farm?
A: . It's information provided by State Farm.

Q: . Okay. Did State Farm give you any training? THE DEPONENT: Like who -- is there somebody specific that you're asking if I've received training from? MR. ROEBIG: I may ask that. BY MR. ROEBIG: . A: . I don't know where they originated from. No.

Q: . Okay. In other words, when you run out of them do you know where to go and get them?
A: . In the folder that's on our computer. They're saved on our computer.

Q: . Okay. And have they -- have those certificates been in use since you started at the Costello Agency?
A: . Yes.

Q: . And they're still in use?
A: . Yes.

Q: . Okay. And does State Farm know that you use those?
A: . I don't know.

Q: . Do you ever transmit those to State Farm?
A: . No.

Q: . Okay. Ever?
A: . No.

Q: . Alright. And what are they used for?
A: . They're used to share a portion of some insurance information in regards to a policy for a customer.

Q: . Okay. But -- and I understand that what you're telling me is that they're used to share information with a customer.
A: . Yes.

Q: . Are they used for any other purpose?
A: . The customers will typically ask for them so they can provide them to an employer or if they're like a contractor to show somebody they're working for that they have insurance on a vehicle.

Q: . So in other words, it's used as proof of insuring coverage? MR. SHAW: Object to form. Go ahead. BY THE DEPONENT:

Q: . Is it your testimony that the Certificate of Liability Insurance is a sample of what might be the coverage?
A: . It's a sample. It's not an all inclusive document. There could be exclusions or endorsements on a policy that would not be included in a Certificate of Insurance.

Q: . Well, I understand that it's not a policy contract in the customary sense that contains all of the coverage positions and exclusions. I understand that. A: . I don't know.

Q: . Who would know?
A: . I'm not sure.

A: . No.

Q: . Okay. So what subset of your clients do you draw a Certificate of Liability Insurance documents up for?
A: . Those that ask for one.

Q: . Okay. What would those be? MR. SHAW: Object to form. BY THE DEPONENT:
A: . To show somebody that they have an insurance policy with liability limits. BY MR. ROEBIG:

A: . When I'm giving somebody a Certificate of Insurance I give them information that might show a portion of the coverage on a policy that they would have in place. BY MR. ROEBIG:

Q: . Okay.
A: . It's not all inclusive and it wouldn't be the final document or final place that I would look to verify information about a policy.

Q: . Okay. But it is you attesting or certifying that the client has liability coverage. Is that right? THE DEPONENT: Are you asking about anyone in particular or just in general for anybody? MR. ROEBIG: Just in general so that I understand the use and significance of that particular document that we're discussing. BY THE DEPONENT:
A: . I would give somebody a Certificate of Insurance to show that they have a policy and some of the coverages and some of what might be included in the policy details. BY MR. ROEBIG:

Q: . Particularly liability coverage?
A: . Liability coverage is the most common thing to put on a Certificate of Insurance.

Q: . Hence the name of the document; Certificate of Liability Insurance. Correct?
A: . Yes. Yes.

Q: . Because some of your clients need to turn that over to employers or partners or the government. Correct?
A: . I don't know who they are always turning it over to but they usually are providing it to somebody.

Q: . And the person to whom they're providing it you understand relies on your certification that they have liability coverage. Yes?
A: . Yes. (Whereupon, Plaintiff's Exhibit No. 1 was marked for identification by the court reporter.) BY MR. ROEBIG:

THE DEPONENT: Sorry. Ask me the question again. BY MR. ROEBIG: . Do all of the Certificates of Liability Insurance that you work with since you got to Costello have the State Farm logo on them?
